## Slice 1 of the Skeleton Object Model — complete

**Files created (all within my assigned dirs):**
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/runtime/skeleton/schema.ts` — TS authoring shapes mirroring the doc: `Vec3/Quat/Transform`, `Joint`+`JointKind`, `Bone`, and the carried-data sections (`Meshes` union per-bone|skinned, `Collider`, `Mount`, `Contact`, `NamedBehavior`, `CapabilityRef`), plus `Skeleton`. Pure declaration helpers `defineSkeleton(...)` and `staticProp(...)`. No validation logic (host-owned).
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/runtime/skeleton/events.ts` — 11 event types via `defineEventType` (`skeleton.bone.add/remove`, `.joint.set`, `.mesh.assign`, `.collision.add`, `.physics.set`, `.animation.set`, `.mount.add`, `.contact.pin`, `.behavior.set`, `.static.set`) + dispatch helpers that emit through editorbus, each carrying the skeleton id as a `{kind:'skeleton'}` TargetRef with finer bone/mount/contact refs.
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/runtime/skeleton/index.ts` — re-export barrel.
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/runtime/skeleton/skeleton.test.ts` — 7-test micro-harness (editorbus.test.ts shape).
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/framework/skeleton/skeleton.zig` — Zig types mirroring the TS shapes.
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/framework/skeleton/bones_loader.zig` — the `validate(alloc, skeleton, hooks) -> Result` validator.
- `/home/siah/creative/reactjit/framework/testing/unit/bones_loader.zig` — 14 accept/reject tests (NOT run, per instructions).

**TS test:** esbuild bundle clean, `tools/v8cli` → **7 passed, 0 failed**.

**Zig ast-check:** all three new files **OK** (zig 0.15.2 at `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/zig`).

**Validator design (no per-type branches):** rejects `empty_formation`, `duplicate_bone_id`, `dangling_parent`, `cycle` (incl. self-parent), `invalid_joint` (non-fixed needs non-zero axis; limits min≤max), and `carried_bone_missing`. Every carried bone-reference (mesh/collider/mount/contact `bone_id`) goes through one uniform `refPresent` predicate — no thing-type branching anywhere. The only `switch` is on the `Meshes` union's data shape (per-bone vs skinned), which the doc defines as data.

**Resolvability hook (slice-1 stub):** `ResolveHooks` with optional `resolve_geometry`/`resolve_capability` callbacks; slice 1 passes `accept_all` (geometry/capability names always accepted). When the registries land, slice 2 passes real resolvers and the loader raises `unresolved_geometry`/`unresolved_capability` without altering the validator's structure. A test proves both the custom-resolver reject and the accept_all pass on the same formation.

**Documented fold point with mesh_import.zig** (as `// INTEGRATION:` in bones_loader.zig, NOT implemented — slice 2): `mesh_import.zig`'s `parseGlb`/`visitNode`/`nodeMatrix` (lines 381-423) already walk the glTF node TRS hierarchy — a GLB *is* a bone formation. The slice-2 adapter maps each glTF node → a `Bone` (node id→bone id, parent node→parent, node TRS→`Transform`) and each node's mesh → `Meshes.per_bone{bone_id, geometry_key}` (the interned ParsedMesh key), then hands the `Skeleton` to `validate`. This module does NOT import or rebuild mesh_import.zig.

**Build wiring the user must add (I cannot edit build.zig)** — one module + test step, matching the mesh-import pattern at build.zig:964. The test imports `@import("bones_loader")`; bones_loader pulls in skeleton.zig via a sibling relative import, so only one module is needed:
```zig
const bones_loader_test_mod = b.createModule(.{
    .root_source_file = b.path("framework/testing/unit/bones_loader.zig"),
    .target = target, .optimize = optimize, .link_libc = true,
});
bones_loader_test_mod.addImport("bones_loader", b.createModule(.{
    .root_source_file = b.path("framework/skeleton/bones_loader.zig"),
    .target = target, .optimize = optimize, .link_libc = true,
}));
const bones_loader_test = b.addTest(.{ .name = "bones-loader-test", .root_module = bones_loader_test_mod });
const bones_loader_test_step = b.step("test-bones-loader", "Run the skeleton validator unit tests");
bones_loader_test_step.dependOn(&b.addRunArtifact(bones_loader_test).step);
```

**Other integration notes:** the editor cart consumes the TS contract via `@reactjit/skeleton`; events flow through the existing `runtime/editorbus` bus (local fallback today, Zig `__editor_bus_*` when workstream A lands). The TargetRef `kind` vocabulary I added (`skeleton`/`bone`/`mount`/`contact`) is owned by this authoring system per the open-vocabulary seam.

**Contract gaps with the doc:** none material. Two shape decisions worth flagging: (1) joint limits are modeled as `limits:{min,max}` in TS and flattened to `limit_min`/`limit_max` optionals in Zig (cleaner default handling); (2) capability params are typed (`Record<string,unknown>`) in TS but carried as opaque `params_json` in Zig, since slice 1 doesn't parse them — that parse is the slice-2 capability-resolution concern.</result>
